finding: The no-own-commit guard lists every reflog entry except `reset:`, `branch:` and any subject containing `Fast-forward`, so it fails both ways. A Diagnosis branch moved to a newer feature tip by `git rebase` (no own commit) still lands and lists a push that shipped no fix. A real fix commit whose message contains `Fast-forward` is refused.
why: ship.py:26-27 states the rule: "Refused too when no commit past the Base commit was made on the Diagnosis branch." The round-3 finding this delta closes (r-005, docs/afk/small-lane/plan/review/0007-ship-script-2cfd96b-r3.findings.json) names "a pull or reset before the fix was committed" and asks for "a `commit` entry for one of those commits". The delta fixed reset and pull, but `rebase (finish)` is a sibling path that keeps the old behaviour.
fix: Match on the reflog action, not a substring, and use an allow-list. Take the text before the first `: ` of `%gs` and count a commit as made only when that action is `commit`, `commit (amend)`, `commit (merge)`, `cherry-pick` or `revert`. Add land tests for a `git rebase` onto a newer feature tip (expect refused) and for a fix commit whose message contains `Fast-forward` (expect done).
evidence: ship.py:658-659 "made = {sha for sha, _, subject in (line.partition(\" \") for line in log.splitlines())\n            if not subject.startswith((\"reset:\", \"branch:\")) and \"Fast-forward\" not in subject}". Probe (scratch test importing scripts/tests/test_ship.py fixtures, git 2.53.0): branch checked out at origin/feat/export, a stranger pushes one commit, then `git rebase -q origin/feat/export`; land answered {'step': 'land', 'status': 'done', 'push': 'feat/export@3d1b6235e3bf...', 'how': 'found'} and listed ['push: feat/export@3d1b6235e3bf...']. The branch reflog for that move is "0aa05966... rebase (finish): refs/heads/fix onto 0aa05966...". Second probe: one commit with message "land checks a Fast-forward push" (reflog "commit: land checks a Fast-forward push"); land answered {'status': 'refused', 'reason': 'none of the 1 commits past the Base commit 048a5901... was made on fix/bug-export-drops-row, so land would ship no fix'}. Also a message-less `git update-ref refs/heads/fix origin/feat` writes a reflog entry with an empty subject, which this guard counts as made.

criterion: Assertion strength: Happy-path-only (Meszaros), the assert cannot tell the intended refusal from another one
finding: The test for `auto` reading the remote's default branch passes even when ship.py never reads that branch. With origin/main deleted and the symbolic-ref read removed, land refuses with the 'names no default branch' message, and that message also contains the substring 'base branch'.
why: Checklist test-veracity.md:9-10: assert on the real observable output and add negative cases. The round 3 fix in skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:25-26 says "`auto` reads as the remote's default branch, main and master"; this test is its only proof.
fix: Assert the specific reason: `assert "develop is the repository's base branch" in result["reason"]`, so the 'names no default branch' refusal fails the test.
evidence: scripts/tests/test_ship.py:885 `assert result["status"] == "refused" and "base branch" in result["reason"], result`; skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:638-639 `raise refuse(f"`git.base-branch` is `auto` and {remote} names no default branch, main or " "master, so land cannot rule out the base branch")`. Mutation probe on a `git archive 9fef6867` snapshot: ship.py:634 replaced by `found = set()` -> all 22 land tests pass.

criterion: Happy-path-only (Meszaros), a new branch with no test
finding: No test proves that `auto` always rules out main and master. Every auto test has a remote-tracking ref for the target branch, so removing `| {"main", "master"}` leaves all land tests green. The unprotected case is a target of main or master whose tracking ref is absent while origin/HEAD names another branch. Land fetches the target only after this check.
why: Checklist test-veracity.md:10 says to add the boundary or negative case for new branching logic. The docstring at skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:630-631 says "the remote's default branch, main and master"; this line implements that promise.
fix: Add a land test that points origin/HEAD at develop, deletes refs/remotes/origin/main, uses Base `main@{commit}`, and asserts the refusal reason "main is the repository's base branch" and an unchanged remote main.
evidence: skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:640 `return found | {"main", "master"}`; scripts/tests/test_ship.py:828-830 (the master case pushes and fetches origin/master first, so `found` already holds master). Mutation probe on the 9fef6867 snapshot: line 640 replaced by `return found` -> all 22 land tests pass.

criterion: Happy-path-only (Meszaros), 2 of 3 reflog exclusions have no test
finding: The made-on-branch filter excludes 3 reflog kinds, but only the `reset:` case has a test. Removing the `branch:` exclusion or the `Fast-forward` exclusion leaves all land tests green. Both paths are real: `git checkout -B fix feat` after feat moved writes `branch: Reset to feat` at the new feature tip, and `git merge --ff-only feat` writes `merge feat: Fast-forward`. Without those exclusions, land treats the other author's commit as the fix and pushes it.
why: Checklist test-veracity.md:10 says to add the negative case for each new branch. The contract docstring at skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:26-27 says land is "Refused too when no commit past the Base commit was made on the Diagnosis branch."
fix: Parametrize this test over 3 ways to take the newer feature tip: `reset --hard`, `checkout -B {BRANCH} origin/{FEATURE}` after the fetch, and `merge --ff-only origin/{FEATURE}`. Each case asserts 'was made on' and an unchanged remote tip.
evidence: skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:659 `if not subject.startswith(("reset:", "branch:")) and "Fast-forward" not in subject}`; scripts/tests/test_ship.py:928 `git(repo, "reset", "-q", "--hard", f"origin/{FEATURE}")` (the only path tested). Scratch repo on git 2.53: reflog shows `08b15b51... branch: Reset to feat` and `08b15b51... merge feat: Fast-forward` at the moved tip. Mutation probe on the 9fef6867 snapshot: `startswith(("reset:",))` -> 22 land tests pass; `Fast-forward` clause removed -> 22 land tests pass.

finding: The new docstring says `afk-config.py detect_base_branch` is where `auto` is read, but that function does not read `auto`. It returns a branch name or `auto` when it scaffolds a new config file. It also takes the first match from `origin` only, not a union from the branch's remote. CONFIG.md owns the meaning of `auto`, and it defines a different set.
why: CONFIG.md:92 "`git.base-branch: auto` resolves to `origin/main`, else `origin/master`, else the branch's upstream, else `HEAD`." AGENTS.md: "State each fact ... in exactly ONE file — its owning file — every other skill *points* by path". LANGUAGE.md §1: "One term, one meaning".
fix: Point the docstring at the correct source, and say that land refuses a set larger than CONFIG.md's: for example "`auto` (CONFIG.md) widened for land: the remote's default branch (as scripts/protected-lookup.py `default_branch` reads it), main and master". Alternatively, update CONFIG.md:92 if the remote default branch belongs to the meaning of `auto` everywhere.
evidence:
ship.py:630-631 """"`auto` as afk-config.py `detect_base_branch` reads it: the remote's default branch, main
    and master; refused when the remote names none of them.""""; scripts/afk-config.py:959-967 "def detect_base_branch(root: Path) -> str:
    """The default branch name, or `auto` when git will not say."""
    head = _git(root, "symbolic-ref", "--quiet", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD")
    if head:
        return head.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    for candidate in ("main", "master"): ... return candidate
    return "auto""; its caller scripts/afk-config.py:1034 "base = detect_base_branch(root)" is the init scaffold.

criterion: Happy-path-only (Meszaros): no off-boundary value around a new comparison
finding: The delta raises the minimum commit-id length from 4 to 7 characters, but no test pins that floor. The only new parse test uses the word `at`, which is not hex, so the old 4-character floor also passes it. A 6-character id, or a hex-only word like `added` before the commit, is never checked.
why: Checklist test-veracity.md:10: "no off-boundary values around new comparisons -> add the boundary/negative cases".
fix: Parametrize test_fast_forward_land_reads_a_base_commit_written_after_a_word with a Base such as `{FEATURE} added at {start}` that must land, plus a 6-character id that must refuse with 'names no commit'.
evidence: skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:284 `commit = re.search(r"\b[0-9a-fA-F]{7,40}\b", rest[0]) if rest else None`; scripts/tests/test_ship.py:914 `path = diagnosis(tmp_path, Base=f"`{FEATURE}` at `{start}`")`. Mutation probe on the 9fef6867 snapshot: `{7,40}` changed to `{4,40}` -> 22 land tests pass.

finding: The test's premise that the remote names no default branch depends on the shared template never having fetched, so it has no refs/remotes/origin/HEAD. The test does not state or set that condition. On git 2.53, one plain fetch creates origin/HEAD. After origin/main is deleted, `symbolic-ref --quiet` still prints refs/remotes/origin/main, so any later fetch added to the shared setup breaks this test for a reason the body does not show.
why: Checklist test-veracity.md:14: "fixture hidden in a file/DB row/shared setup (mystery guest) ... relevant fixture inline".
fix: Set up the premise inline: run `git(repo, "symbolic-ref", "--delete", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD")` with check=False, or assert that it is absent, before deleting refs/remotes/origin/main.
evidence: scripts/tests/test_ship.py:892 `git(repo, "update-ref", "-d", "refs/remotes/origin/main")`; scripts/tests/test_ship.py:99-111 (the template clones an empty bare repo and never fetches). Scratch repo on git 2.53: before fetch, `symbolic-ref` rc=1; after `git fetch`, it prints `refs/remotes/origin/main` rc=0; after `update-ref -d refs/remotes/origin/main`, it still prints `refs/remotes/origin/main` rc=0.
